title: The lost report
summary: The CEO's precious Biscuit Index report is lost on a shared drive with 300 files. Hunt by name, size, age and content with find, wildcards and grep.

nodes.custard: the file server holding the company shared drive, /srv/shared

tasks.title: Count the spreadsheets
tasks.text: Warm-up. Finance wants to know how many `.csv` exports are on the shared drive `/srv/shared`, in any folder at any depth. How many?
hints: `find /srv/shared -name '*.csv'` lists every file whose name ends in `.csv`. Keep the quotes: they stop the shell expanding `*` itself.
Pipe the list into a line counter: `find /srv/shared -name '*.csv' | wc -l`.

tasks.title: Who is hogging the drive?
tasks.text: One file is far bigger than everything else: more than 5 MB, when most files are a few hundred bytes. What is its **name**?
hints: `find` can filter by size: `-size +5M` means bigger than 5 megabytes (`k` for kilobytes, `G` for gigabytes).
`find /srv/shared -size +5M`, and `ls -lh` on the result shows its size in human units.

tasks.title: Who touched what yesterday?
tasks.text: Brenda says someone edited a finance file **yesterday**. Every other file is weeks or months old. Submit the **full path** of the file modified within the last 2 days.
hints: `-mtime` filters by modification time in days: `-mtime -2` is less than 2 days ago, `-mtime +30` more than 30.
Add `-type f` so only files show up: `find /srv/shared -type f -mtime -2`.

tasks.title: Find the Biscuit Index
tasks.text: Now the real hunt. Nobody remembers what the report file is called, only that it contains the line `Biscuit Index Q3: <number>`. What is the Q3 number?
hints: File names won't help: search the **contents**. `grep 'text' file` prints the lines of a file that contain `text`.
`grep -r` searches every file in a folder tree: `grep -r 'Biscuit Index' /srv/shared`. Careful: there is an old Q2 draft too.
`grep -rn 'Biscuit Index Q3' /srv/shared` also shows the line number. `-l` would print only the file names.

tasks.title: Back up the spreadsheets
tasks.text: Before anyone "tidies up", copy **every** `.csv` file from anywhere under `/srv/shared` into one folder, `/root/csv-backup` (all side by side, no subfolders). The originals stay where they are.

checks.fail_msg: /root/csv-backup does not hold all of the .csv files (directly inside it) yet.
Some originals are gone from /srv/shared. Copy, don't move! Restart the lab to get them back.

hints: `mkdir /root/csv-backup` first. `cp file folder/` copies a file into a folder.
`find` can run a command for each file it finds: `find /srv/shared -name '*.csv' -exec cp {} /root/csv-backup/ \;` (`{}` becomes the file name, `\;` ends the command).

tasks.title: Sweep up the crumbs
tasks.text: Gary's editor left `autosave-NN.tmp` files all over the drive. Delete **every** file ending in `.tmp` under `/srv/shared`, and nothing else. (Gary's `tmp-notes.txt` must survive: it only *looks* like junk.)

checks.fail_msg: Too much got deleted (tmp-notes.txt, a .csv or the report is gone). Restart the lab and try a more precise pattern.

hints: Look before you delete: `find /srv/shared -name '*.tmp'` shows exactly what would go. Does `tmp-notes.txt` match `*.tmp`? (No: the pattern says *ends* in .tmp.)
Happy with the list? Add `-delete` at the end: `find /srv/shared -name '*.tmp' -delete`. There is no recycle bin on Linux, so always run without `-delete` first.
